title: Book Two · Chapter 139: A Refund Line
story:
One evening, Dad has an old envelope beside his cup. There is a small sum of money inside and a name on the front.

“Another bill?” Ronan asks.

“A last payment back,” Dad says. “From an old job.”

“From the shop?”

“Yes.”

Ronan sits down. Mum checks the name against a page in the brown notebook. Dad counts the money.

“I thought the shop was finished.”

“We no longer use the shop. But I still need to return money for some old jobs.”

Dad shows him the line in the notebook. One column says REFUND. It shows how much Dad must return. Beside it are three smaller payments. Dad adds today's amount in the last blank space.

“Is all of it paid now?”

“For this job, yes.”

“All the jobs?”

Dad turns to another page. “Not this whole book. And not all in the same way. Some needed work. Some needed money back.”

Ronan stares at the columns. He wants a last page that ends everything.

“Will we always be doing this?”

“Not always.”

“When will it end?”

“I cannot give you one day tonight.”

Ronan pushes his chair back. “You always have a number for a shelf.”

“Because I can measure a shelf.”

Ronan looks around the room. His school book is beside the window. Mum's work basket is under her chair.

“I thought we might have to leave again,” he says.

Dad looks at him.

“Is that what you were asking?”

“Part of it.”

Ronan keeps one hand on the chair back. He remembers the red bike leaving before the move.

“I see another envelope and think about the old house.”

Mum reaches for the household book.

Dad does not tell Ronan to stop remembering. He puts the refund envelope beside the notebook, away from the supper space.

“We are making this payment as we agreed,” he says.

Ronan looks at the line. He cannot see a whole future from it. He can see the customer's name on the envelope.

His face is still warm. He wants to understand the plan, and he wants an answer bigger than the plan can give him.

Mum puts the household book beside the old account book. She keeps one hand near it.

Mum puts a hand on the notebook before the talk grows louder.

“We can show you our plan,” she says. “We cannot show you a day we do not know.”

She opens their household page. The page has money for food, rent, work costs, and agreed return payments. Ronan reads the headings. He cannot remember every amount at once.

“Does my bread money help?”

“Your bread money is for bread,” Mum says.

Dad seals the envelope. He writes the date below the name.

Ronan looks at his hands. “I do not like this book.”

“Neither do I,” Dad says. “I still need it.”

For a while the three of them are silent. Then Mum asks Dad to move the cup so she can put supper down.

Dad does it. Ronan brings the bowls.

After supper, Dad takes the envelope to the agreed person near Mr Sun's shop. Ronan walks with him as far as the wide road. They talk about the cooler air, then about a man carrying a very long broom.

“Enough for the whole street,” Dad says.

“Not if he misses the corners.”

Dad smiles. At the crossing, Ronan turns home. Dad goes on with the envelope. Dad still has other lines to finish in the old book. Tonight he will finish paying for this one job. Mum leaves the door open for both of them.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

refund＝返款；seal＝封好；household＝家庭的；measure＝测量。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么关店不等于旧责任全结束？
2. 父母怎样说明知道的计划和不知道的日期？

## 读句子

**Dad / seals / the envelope.** Dad／封好／信封。
